(a) Through September 25, 2017.—During the period beginning on the date of the enactment of this Act and ending on September 25, 2017, the second sentence of section 3684(c) of title 38, United States Code, shall be applied—
        (1) by substituting “$6” for “$12”; and 
        (2) by substituting “$12” for “$15”.  
    (b) September 26, 2017, Through September 25, 2026.—During the period beginning on September 26, 2017, and ending on September 25, 2026, the second sentence of such section shall be applied—

    (c) Conforming Amendment.—Section 406 of the Department of Veterans Affairs Expiring Authorities Act of 2014 (Public Law 113–175; 38 U.S.C. 3684 note), as amended by the Department of Veterans Affairs Expiring Authorities Act of 2016, is amended by striking “During the three-year period beginning on the date of the enactment of this Act” and inserting “During the period beginning on the date of the enactment of this Act and ending on the day before the date of the enactment of the Jeff Miller and Richard Blumenthal Veterans Health Care and Benefits Improvement Act of 2016”.

fable.w: This section only temporarily substitutes dollar amounts in 38 U.S.C. 3684(c) (reporting fees paid to educational institutions) and makes a conforming amendment. The only possible hook is that the fees relate to outside institutions, but nothing here has the federal government consulting, hearing from, or being sued by any outside party, and no rulemaking, comment period, or advisory body is involved. It is a purely technical payment-amount adjustment.

qwen_block.w: This section merely adjusts monetary amounts in a statute through temporary amendments. It does not involve any consultation, coordination, or decision-making process with parties outside the federal government. There are no advisory boards, public hearings, comment periods, or rights to sue mentioned.
qwen_block.s: (a) Through September 25, 2017.—During the period beginning on the date of the enactment of this Act and ending on September 25, 2017, the second sentence of section 3684(c) of title 38, United States Code, shall be applied— (1) by substituting “$6” for “$12”; and (2) by substituting “$12” for “$15”.

opus.w: This section only changes the dollar amounts in 38 U.S.C. 3684(c) for set time periods and fixes the dates in an earlier Act. It does not ask for input from states, experts, the public or anyone else outside the federal government. Even if the underlying statute involves schools reporting to the VA, this text creates no consultation, comment period, hearing, rulemaking authority or right to sue.
opus.s:
the second sentence of section 3684(c) of title 38, United States Code, shall be applied—
        (1) by substituting “$6” for “$12”; and 
        (2) by substituting “$12” for “$15”.
opus.b:
The section changes the dollar amounts in 38 U.S.C. 3684(c), the reporting fees the VA pays to educational institutions, for two time periods. It also makes a conforming amendment to an earlier Act's dates.

The tempting reading is to treat the institutions' reports to the VA (under § 3684) as outsiders interacting with the government. That fails because this text only swaps out fee amounts. It does not set up any consultation, hearing, comment period, rulemaking, advisory body or right to sue over a federal decision.

qwen_chat.w: This section amends statutory dollar amounts for veterans' benefits. It does not require consultation, public comment, or coordination with any outside party (such as veterans, states, or experts) before the decision is made. The definition explicitly excludes applications for benefits, and this text describes a mechanical adjustment to benefit formulas rather than a participatory process.
qwen_chat.s: (a) Through September 25, 2017.—During the period beginning on the date of the enactment of this Act and ending on September 25, 2017, the second sentence of section 3684(c) of title 38, United States Code, shall be applied— (1) by substituting “$6” for “$12”; and (2) by substituting “$12” for “$15”.
qwen_chat.b: Tempting-but-wrong reading: One might argue that changing dollar amounts affects veterans (outside the government), so it involves them. However, the definition explicitly excludes applications for benefits or grants, and this section merely adjusts statutory parameters for benefit calculations without requiring any consultation, comment period, or interaction with veterans or other outside parties. The process is purely internal legislative/administrative adjustment.
